text:
In consulting, frontend performance isn’t just a technical hurdle—it’s a business imperative. Last quarter, a client’s dashboard load time averaged 5.2 seconds, pushing bounce rates past 40%. We needed a strategy that balanced speed with scalability, without overhauling their entire stack.  

The problem was twofold: legacy assets bloated the bundle size, and inefficient API calls compounded latency. Even with a React-based UI, the framework wasn’t the bottleneck—it was how we leveraged it. Without clear performance budgets or automated testing, we risked shipping subpar experiences under tight deadlines.  

Start by auditing with Lighthouse and Chrome DevTools. Set a baseline: bundle size under 2MB, first contentful paint under 2.5s, and CLS below 0.1. Use a staging environment mirroring production traffic, and integrate Web Vitals tracking. For REST APIs, enforce 200ms response time thresholds using Apollo Client with error boundaries. TypeScript can catch type-related performance pitfalls early, so ensure your config enforces strict mode and minimizes runtime checks.  

First, optimize assets. Use WebP for images and implement lazy loading with IntersectionObserver. Split React components into chunks using code splitting and dynamic imports. For APIs, cache frequent endpoints with Redis and paginate results to reduce payload size. In TypeScript, define utility types for API responses to enforce structure and avoid unnecessary data fetching.  

After implementing these changes, the dashboard’s load time dropped to 1.8s, and CLS improved to 0.05. Lighthouse scores jumped from 68 to 92, while server response times stabilized at 150ms. Bounce rates fell to 18%, and the client’s internal tooling saw a 30% increase in feature adoption.  

Performance gains here weren’t accidental—they were the result of intentional architecture choices. Prioritize tooling that aligns with project constraints, and don’t shy away from rethinking how frameworks like React or REST APIs are used.  

For deeper dives, check out the Web Vitals specification, React’s performance hooks, and TypeScript’s advanced type inference techniques. Also, explore how REST APIs can be optimized with GraphQL where appropriate. The goal isn’t just speed—it’s sustainable, scalable speed that meets client needs without compromising developer efficiency.
